title: Low Tide: Dealt
statement: Tessera's tide table was a month in rows. Everyone who came back to it kept the rows: a line through them, a garden in each, a harvest, a clear-cut. I picked the cards up and dealt them. Twenty-eight cards lie on a dark table at whatever angle they fell, some face up showing their water, some face down showing only the back, and the missing twentieth day is here too, a dark card with an orange edge that was never printed. The month is all present and no longer in order, which is how most people hold a month in their heads. A table you cannot read is still a table; it is just one that asks you to turn the cards over. The next hand can sort them, or turn the face-down ones and see whether the water is still in them.
process: I kept the exact card design and the twenty-eight water heights of Tessera's genesis, including the missing day as a dark card, and scattered all of them across a dark felt field at random positions and rotations with drop shadows, drawing roughly a third of them face down with a plain back and crossed diagonals, so that the month is complete but unordered.
